title: Partner Solutions Architect, Billing

title: Regulatory Reporting Program Manager, Stablecoin
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Stripe provides regulated payments and financial services products, and also has a number of regulated subsidiaries, including in the United States (Money Transmitter and lending licenses). These licenses have programs of periodic and ad hoc regulatory reporting stemming from license requirements, and are critical aspects of the supervisory mechanisms for these entities. The Global Regulatory Reporting team leads the process by which we report regulatory data externally to regulators in support of our payments licenses.
What you'll do
In this role, you'll support the Global Regulatory Reporting team by partnering with Legal, Compliance, Accounting, Business and Product, and Data Analytics teams across Stripe to maintain the Stripe North American regulatory reporting program. This includes understanding and documenting the applicable regulatory reporting requirements in the region, implementing systems and processes for comprehensively tracking those requirements for each of the Stripe North American entities, maintaining the end-to-end processes for the collation of data, production of reports, and continuously monitoring compliance to meet the expectations of regulators.
Stripe is both a technology company and a financial services company, and you'll need to be comfortable straddling both of those worlds every day. You'll enjoy dealing with that puzzle, seeking creative solutions and moving quickly, often in the face of ambiguity.
Responsibilities
Own end-to-end U.S. regulatory reporting program for digital assets including stablecoin-related financial activities, including defining reporting scope, governance, timelines, and accountability across required regulatory filings
Interpret U.S. regulatory reporting requirements applicable to stablecoins, digital assets, payments, and custody, and translate them into clear reporting specifications, data definitions, and execution plans in partnership with Legal and Compliance
Manage the full regulatory reporting lifecycle, from data sourcing and aggregation through validation, internal review, sign-off, and timely submission to regulators
Ensure regulatory reports accurately reflect stablecoin-specific activities and risks, including issuance, redemption, circulation, reserves, custody arrangements, and transaction flows across on-chain and off-chain systems
Design and maintain a robust regulatory reporting control framework, including data quality checks, reconciliations, documentation, and issue remediation to support audit and exam readiness
Partner with Engineering, Data, Finance, Compliance, and Legal to improve data lineage, transparency, and automation across regulatory reporting processes as the business scales
Own regulatory reporting change management, including assessing the impact of new or evolving stablecoin regulations, product launches, and system changes on reporting scope, data requirements, and controls
Develop and maintain regulator-ready documentation, including reporting methodologies, assumptions, data lineage, and process documentation to support supervisory reviews and examinations
Serve as the primary point of contact for regulatory reporting matters during U.S. regulatory exams, audits, and regulatory inquiries
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field; equivalent practical experience in financial services regulatory reporting will be considered
4+ years of experience leading the delivery of an ongoing regulatory reporting program within a regulated financial services environment, ideally supporting stablecoin issuance, payments, or custody-related activities
Strong understanding of U.S. compliance and regulatory obligations applicable to stablecoins, including evolving federal and state frameworks (including, but not limited to, the GENIUS Act and related Treasury, banking, and payments guidance)
Excellent working knowledge of the U.S. payment stablecoin regulatory landscape, with experience engaging directly with U.S. federal regulators (e.g., OCC, Treasury) and state regulators on regulatory reporting, data submissions, or supervisory requests
Demonstrated ability to work across complex data environments, including navigating on-chain and off-chain data sources, internal ledgers, and third-party systems to produce accurate, cohesive, and regulator-ready reporting deliverables
Experience reading, analyzing, and compiling financial statements, reserve-related data, transaction-level reporting, and other financial regulatory reports relevant to stablecoin and payments activity
Background in financial services with direct exposure to stablecoins, digital assets, payments, e-money, or other money services business activities
Demonstrated success executing complex, cross-functional programs in fast-growing organizations, with an emphasis on building scalable, repeatable regulatory reporting processes
Strong analytical skills and judgment, with the ability to quickly understand novel or ambiguous regulatory and data challenges and drive balanced, risk-aware solutions
Ability to operate independently and efficiently in a fast-paced, high-volume, and evolving regulatory environment
Proven ability to collaborate effectively across Compliance, Legal, Finance, Engineering, Data, Product, and Accounting teams
A strong “culture of compliance” mindset, with the ability to translate regulatory expectations into practical, business-aligned execution without impeding responsible growth
Preferred qualifications
Experience with stablecoins, digital assets, payments, or fintech platforms
Familiarity with regulatory reporting for banks, trust companies, payment institutions, or money services businesses
Experience working on Call Reports FFIEC041 and FFIEC031
Experience supporting regulatory exams, audits, or supervisory reviews
Exposure to reporting automation, data pipelines, or reporting tools

title: Container Engineer
description:
ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. More than 9 million developers and 250,000+ customers now build on Supabase, and the majority of new databases on the platform are created by AI app builders — so the systems underneath have to stay reliable while they grow fast.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Container Engineering (ConEng) owns the internal container platform that runs Supabase's multi-tenant, multi-region services — the managed Kubernetes platform that other engineering teams build and deploy on top of. We own cluster lifecycle and cluster classes, multi-cluster and multi-region topology, capacity, scheduling, isolation and runtime safety, the higher-level platform APIs, the Kubernetes deployment contract and Argo semantics, rollout primitives, and runtime configuration and secret injection.

 

Your job is to make the platform itself trustworthy, observable, and cheap to operate at scale — and to raise the reliability bar for everyone who depends on it. This is not a gatekeeper role. You'll make the reliable path the easy path: building the automation and platform APIs that let product teams run safely by default, instrumenting what we operate, and making sure that when something breaks we detect it and recover fast.

 

The work spans three strength areas:

Tooling & ecosystem — deep knowledge of the container and orchestration landscape (Kubernetes, containerd/OCI, the CNCF ecosystem) and a clear point of view on how to compose it.

Software engineering — designing and building the platform's automation, controllers, and internal tooling as production code, including solutions that don't come pre-shaped by an existing tool.

Operational / SRE practice — the discipline (SLOs, error budgets, incident response, ORRs) that runs the platform at scale as a predictable one.

We expect you to be genuinely deep in at least one of these, and many of our strongest candidates are deep in two (usually leaning toward one). Bringing real strength across all three is rare and exceptional — and even then, no one is equally strong in all three at once, so you'd focus where you're most needed at any given time. Different profiles are welcome here; tell us which of these is your center of gravity.




WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

Regardless of the skill set, all team members carry a share of the team's on-call rota, responding to platform incidents and driving them to resolution and follow-up.

Platform reliability & operations

 - Define SLIs/SLOs and error budgets for the container platform itself, and build error-budget policies that actually gate platform changes.

 - Own the Operational Readiness Review (ORR) process for new platform capabilities and major changes.

 - Design and track metrics for platform uptime, and increase observability into the platform by capturing the right metrics, logs, and traces across the platform layers.

 - Drive the incident-to-improvement pipeline: facilitate blameless postmortems, connect findings to readiness gaps, spot repeat failure patterns, and push through systemic fixes.

Software engineering

 - Build and maintain the platform's automation, controllers, operators, and internal tooling — writing production code and shipping it, not just wiring together existing tools.

 - Design and implement the platform-side CI/CD and rollout primitives that speed up platform deployments while working within proper change and release management.

 - Implement and maintain security automation for the platform: intrusion detection, automated remediation, and patch management.

 - Identify and quantify operational toil, and build the automation that removes it rather than just documenting it.

 - Contribute to the platform's continual testing automation — the test suites and pipelines that validate platform releases are fit for purpose before they reach tenants.

Tooling, ecosystem & architecture

 - Act as a platform reliability and architecture expert — contribute to failure-mode analysis, dependency mapping, and resilience design for multi-tenant container workloads.

 - Evaluate and evolve the platform's tooling ecosystem (orchestration, runtime, networking, isolation, and observability stack) with a clear, opinionated view on trade-offs.

 - Improve system architecture to reduce infrastructure cost while balancing security, reliability, and performance across tenants.

 - Guide teams building on the platform to design sustainable on-call practices for their own services: alert quality, escalation paths, runbook coverage, and noise reduction.

 


YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

 - Have 5+ years in platform engineering, container/Kubernetes platform operations, SRE, or production infrastructure, and have operated production systems at scale and carried on-call for them.

 - Are genuinely deep in at least one — ideally two — of the three strength areas below (and tell us which is your center of gravity):

 - Tooling & ecosystem — know the container/orchestration landscape well: Kubernetes, containerd and the OCI/CRI standards, and the surrounding CNCF ecosystem (e.g. Argo CD/Argo Rollouts for GitOps and progressive delivery; Cilium/eBPF networking and the Gateway API; Karpenter/KEDA-style autoscaling; and workload-isolation runtimes such as gVisor or Kata Containers). You reason about trade-offs rather than reaching for defaults.

 - Software engineering — write real production code (Go and/or a comparable systems language) and can build controllers, operators, and platform APIs — stepping back to the underlying problem and building the right solution when no off-the-shelf tool fits.

 - Operational / SRE practice — are fluent in SLOs, error budgets, and operational KPIs; have led incident response and blameless postmortems; and have driven down MTTD/MTTR for systems you operated.

 - Have worked with large-scale multi-tenant systems and understand isolation as a spectrum — from namespaces, RBAC, network policies, and resource quotas through to stronger primitives such as virtual clusters (e.g. vCluster) or VM-class runtimes.

 - Operate confidently on AWS (multiple accounts, IAM, VPC) and are comfortable with infrastructure-as-code (Pulumi preferred; Terraform/CDK also fine) and Kubernetes.

 - Script and automate to eliminate toil rather than absorb it.

 - Communicate clearly with both infrastructure specialists and product engineers, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

 - Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and iterating toward better systems over time.

Nice to Have

 - Experience building and operating a multi-tenant Kubernetes platform that internal teams deploy onto.

 - Familiarity with policy engines (Kyverno, or OPA/Gatekeeper) and cost-attribution tooling (OpenCost/Kubecost) for per-tenant chargeback/showback.

 - Experience with managed database platforms or Postgres.

 - Familiarity with OpenTelemetry, Prometheus/VictoriaMetrics, Grafana, or similar observability tooling.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Fully Remote
   
   We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

 - ESOP
   
   Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

 - Tech Allowance
   
   Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

 - Health Benefits
   
   Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

 - Annual Off-Sites
   
   Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

 - Flexible Work
   
   We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

 - Professional Development
   
   Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.
   
   


ABOUT THE TEAM

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

 - ~400 team members

 - 60+ countries

 - 20+ languages spoken

 - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

 - 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

description:

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Equity is a big part of how we reward the people building ElevenLabs, and the programme is growing fast across many countries. You'll own the day-to-day running of it: keeping our cap table accurate and audit-ready, and making sure every grant, exercise and leaver is handled correctly and on time.

You'll work with Finance, Legal and People to turn board-approved decisions into clean records and clear communication. That includes issuing grants, supporting 409A and local valuations, and answering employee questions about their equity.

We're looking for someone who is meticulous about the numbers and who treats employees as customers. You'll find ways to automate the repetitive work, using AI wherever it makes things faster and more reliable.




REQUIREMENTS

 - Hands-on experience administering equity in a cap table or stock plan platform such as Carta, including grants, vesting, exercises, terminations, settlements and reconciliations.

 - Experience administering equity across multiple jurisdictions, including tracking globally mobile participants and coordinating with Tax and Payroll.

description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT RAMP LABS

Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research and engineering group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 85,000+ companies use to move money.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Most agent work today is one agent, one trace, and a person reads the result. We're building systems where that stops working: thousands of agents fanned out over a large search space, each returning partial results, with an orchestrator that turns all of it into something useful: hundreds of merged PRs, a dataset, the input to another system, or something nobody has built yet.

You'll design and run those systems: how work gets split, how agents coordinate, how results get deduplicated, verified and ranked, and what it all costs. The problems are general (agent swarms, agentic map-reduce, long-running fan-out workflows) and you'll own them from prototype to production.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Decide how the work gets done: how to break a problem down, what each agent sees, how many agents to run, and which model handles which step

 - Squeeze accuracy out of the models: context design, self-verification, voting and consensus across agents, and knowing when more agents stop helping

 - Measure quality without reading every trace: sampling, automated verification, and precision and recall on the final output

 - Drive down cost and latency per useful result: model routing, caching, early stopping, and smaller or fine-tuned models where they hold up

 - Turn one-off experiments into reusable workflows on our existing orchestration stack

 - Evaluate new models, inference setups and training approaches, and bring in what works




WHAT YOU NEED

 - Experience building applied AI systems and LLM applications that shipped

 - Hands-on experience with multi-agent or high-fan-out LLM workloads: parallel agents, map-reduce over models, large batch inference

 - Strong engineering in Python; you build concurrent, distributed systems that hold up in production

 - Judgment about output: you decide what the end result should look like before you scale the swarm, and you can separate signal from agent noise

 - The habit of measuring: cost, yield, false-positive rate, and whether a change actually helped

 - Ownership: you can run a roadmap and a production system with little oversight

 - Clear written communication




NICE-TO-HAVE

 - Used LLMs to search large spaces: codebases, document sets, logs or other large corpora

title: Principal Designer
description:
LIFE AT UIPATH

The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.

To make that happen, we need people who are curious, self-propelled, generous, and genuine. People who love being part of a fast-moving, fast-thinking growth company. And people who care—about each other, about UiPath, and about our larger purpose.

Could that be you?



Principal Product Designer, Platform

Full time · Hybrid (3 days per week onsite)
Bellevue, WA or Austin, TX 


About the team

Within the UiPath Platform, Maestro is our orchestration layer: where agents, robots, and people are brought together to run business processes end to end, and where those processes are designed, built, and deployed.

Maestro is tackling a new class of design problems: how people, agents, and automation work together in complex business processes. You'll help define the interaction models for that world, not just apply patterns that already exist.

We are making the AI surfaces that a new generation of builders work in—people who move between intent, design, and running software without changing tools. And we build Maestro as a deeply integrated team, where design, product management, and engineering share the work and blur the lines between roles.

About the role

You will own the end-to-end experience of one or more Maestro products, from enterprise developer surfaces, through observability, to the consumer-grade business apps our customers rely on to get their work done. You meet with customers to understand their goals deeply, so you know where the product needs to go.

PMs and engineers are your crew. You work with them every day and ship together. The lines between roles are blurring on purpose, but the quality of the experience is yours to own.

You will ship what you design. Designers here use tools like Claude Code and Codex to turn an idea into a working prototype the same day and a shipped feature in days or weeks. You explore in the real product instead of stopping at a mockup, and when it is right, you can open the PR yourself alongside engineering.

When a hard problem cuts across product, engineering, and design, you bring the team to a decision. Your impact extends beyond your own product: you raise the quality bar, shape how we build, and make the designers around you better.

You will report to the Director of Product Design for Maestro.

What you'll own

 - The experience. The end-to-end UX of one or more Maestro products and the quality bar they are held to.

 - Design direction. You set it with your PM and engineering partners, carry it through delivery, and resolve the gaps when the three functions see the problem differently.

 - Coherence across Maestro. What you build on your products has to hold up alongside the others. You work with fellow Maestro and platform designers to ensure consistency.

We use Claude as our primary tool across every part of the job: it drives our static analysis, drafts and fixes vulnerabilities as pull requests, performs first-line bug bounty triage, and assists threat modeling for design reviews. The human work is the judgment layer — system-level reasoning, deciding what matters, and building the next thing the model can't do yet.
This is a builder's role on a senior team. We hire engineers who ship production systems and clear a hands-on threat-modeling bar — people who can find the vulnerability but would rather build the system that finds them all. Every engineer owns a system end-to-end, and the team's work has shaped customer-facing product security — including Claude Code's security review tooling, its security guidance plugin, sandboxing, and auto mode.

Design, build, and operate Claude-powered security systems — LLM-driven code analysis, automated vulnerability remediation, AI-assisted threat modeling — and own one or more of them end-to-end, including the cross-functional relationships that come with it
Lead secure design reviews and threat modeling for novel AI systems, identifying risks that don't map to existing frameworks
Evolve a public bug bounty program where automation handles routine triage and root-cause work, and engineers handle escalations and corner cases
Partner with Product, Infrastructure, and Research teams as an embedded security owner — consulting on launches, shaping architecture, and influencing decisions where security is the constraint
Share an operational on-run rotation with the rest of the team — bounty escalations, incident response, and launch consults on systems serving Claude in production

Production-quality coding ability in at least one of Python, Go, Rust, or TypeScript, with a track record of building durable systems rather than one-off scripts
Practical threat-modeling and vulnerability-identification skills — you've found and reasoned about real bugs in real systems, even if breaking isn't your primary mode
Demonstrated ability to operate with high autonomy and ambiguity — comfortable being handed a problem and a lot of latitude rather than a spec
Clear technical communication with both engineers and leadership
Preferred qualifications:
7+ years in application security, security engineering, or security-focused software engineering
Already use LLMs as a core part of how you work, with opinions about where they help and where they don't
Experience securing agentic, code-execution, or LLM-integrated systems specifically
Prior ownership of a bug bounty program, vulnerability disclosure program, or vulnerability-management infrastructure at scale
Background building security automation or developer-facing security tooling

Discovering new creator growth channels – from social platforms to community groups
Designing growth experiments and campaigns to bring new creators into the Meesho ecosystem
Activating and enabling creators to consistently participate in content commerce by building toolkits, incentives, and playbooks
Collaborating cross-functionally with internal teams (product, ops, tech, creative) and external partners to drive outcomes.

3-4 years of experience in managing digital performance campaigns (Meta ads and Google Ads is preferred)

Organizational skills Excellent communication skills, written and verbal
